page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column. Running head at the top, with the page number at the left. Below the first paragraph, a heading (Articulus IX) with its title in two lines. Then one paragraph, ending with a catchword at the right below the last line. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: Si quæras qui fiat, ut alias nebula in nubem feratur;
quod signum est pluviæ, alias descendens serenitatis
sit nuncia, existimo hanc esse discriminis cau-
sam; Si frigida illa corpuscula de quibus egimus, in
aërem superiorem elevata validè congregatis illis va-
poribus resistant, eos in guttulas minutim coactos
descendere; sin minus impediant, ascendere. Magni
ad utrumque esse momenti Solis accessum, qui si fri-
gida illa corpora repellat, transitu aperto, vapores
ascendere, sin minus valeat; vapores illos citius co-
gere, ac depellere, nedum ad ascendendum juvare.
Ratio hæc est. Quoniam radii Solares cum sint igni-
culi, ut ex Antiquis diximus, id clarius probaturi,
dum ex adversum corporibus illis frigidis vim infe-
runt, ea verò resistunt; fit major viæ[?] compressio,
atque coarctatio. Hinc accidit, quod in partis in-
flammatæ refrigerio unguentum ex calidis, frigidis-
que partibus constans efficit. Calidæ enim partes
poros diducentes ignem ad se proliciunt; frigidæ
verò reliquum partis offensæ motum sedant. Non
absimili, inquam, ratione; vaporum constructione
radii Solaris igneam vaporum materiam ad se tra-
hunt, frigus verò reliquam materiam condensat.
Quomodo etiam Sol validus possit eos vapores de-
pellere, patebit ex proximè dicendis.
ARTICULUS IX.
Cur sub Zona qua vocatur torrida,
singulis diebus pluat.
ADmiratione plenum est quod ferunt de natura illius Zonæ quam antiqui torridam vocabant, rati
ob Solis viciniam, eam igne torreri perpetuo,
ac propterea inhabitabilem. Experientia verò nostri
sæculi demonstrans quam vani sint hominum sensus,

page.notes: Printed long s (s) normalised to s throughout. Initial "A" of the first word of the second paragraph is a large letter, joined as "ADmiratione". "viæ" in the fourth sentence of the first paragraph is doubtful: the word is read as "viæ" but could be "vis" or "viæ" in a smudged print; marked [?]. The final line of the page carries only the catchword "rum", which is the start of "verum", so the paragraph ends on the half word "ve-". Greek and Hebrew: none on this page. Marginal notes: none.
